newsitem.title: UK: Thai sugar output unlikely to exceed last year - Man.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar output unlikely to exceed last year - Man.

text.p: Thailand's sugar output and cane tonnage is unlikely to exceed last year's levels as the crop nears its end and crushing mills close down, E D & F Man said in its latest monthly report on Tuesday.

"With latest reports suggesting that mills are closing apace, it is looking increasingly unlikely that this year's tonnage of cane will exceed last year's final figure of 57.7 million tonnes after all," Man said.
This year's lower yields indicated that sugar output was likely to finish below last year's final figure of just under 6.0 million tonnes tel quel, it added.
It noted that the rate of daily sugar production was falling and sugar content in cane continued to be lower than last season.
Citing current percentages for content and yield versus those at the equivalent stage in 1996, Man said it was unlikely they could catch up with last season in the remaining time available.
Shipments to the end of March were behind those of last year with almost half exported as white sugar.
The overall fall was accounted for by slower raws shipments with last year's major buyers, China and the Philippines, almost totally absent, Man said.
But raws shipments were expected to pick up in the second quarter whilst with the bulk of the whites commitments to Indonesia satisfied, whites should slow down, it added.
